title: Bill Johnson, Bobby Smith and the band's books
summary: Johnson brought 'Cherry' and Smith wrote; Hawkins had two sets of books of 1,000 tunes.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Now, what about your arrangers? You said earlier that you, with Avery Parrish and Sammy Lowe that you had showed them some of your ideas working with lead sheets and things like that. What about Bill Johnson?
Bill Johnson came in. I don't know, have you ever heard of a band, C.S. Belton through those years? Well, they were

down South.
Well, he was with them. So, I
added him here in New York. And, he was writing
with Bill. Bill Johnson was, he was writing with
then. Bill Johnson's a good writer, had his
own, cause he was one of the main, on the Junc-
tion. You know.

And he did, he brought
"Cherry" In The Band from him which was Don
Redman
Bennett's tune. But, he said Hawk, here's a
arrangement
(inaudible) I want you to play for me, "Cherry".
Now, that was down in the beginning of my book.
That was 13 in my book. I'll never forget it.
And, he got a lot, a few other compositions in
there.

Bill, Bill was, I liked Bill. Bill
was terrific. He did some very good piano work.
But, he was doing all that before he joined me.
I'm trying to think who else was in
there. So, he went out and got his own group
later. That's when I brought in Bobby Smith.
He went, he stayed, he spent a lot of time in
Canada. After, he was away from me.
And, Bobby Smith joined. Bobby did a lot of writing. He was a writer when he came in, on his own.

So, I didn't have nothing else to do with it. All that time, I just sat back then. You know, all of them had their ideas, and we rehearsed so many times a week. And when each one of them would bring in an arrangement. I had like 3 and 4 arrangements new a week. They wrote one in a week. So, I had some times 1 and 2 good, and maybe two.

So, I was, I had 2 set of books. All of them went up to 1,000 tunes in each set. That's how many tunes I had. And, I had a lot of original things. When I record, when they'd bring an original tune, if I liked it and I saw possibility, I'd go down and I'd record it for them. You know, I did a lot of original recording. So, if they, they made big, they'd stay there on top.
